Why these conversations can feel difficult.

You may be unsure how to ask, worried about being misunderstood, or used to keeping these topics private. Berkeley UHS recognizes that conversations about sexual health can be challenging.

Start with the experience that feels familiar. You can choose how much to share and practice at your own pace.

Our evidence and approach

Family & culture

You may have learned to keep these topics private. You can start with one need without explaining your whole background. People within the same family or community may feel differently.

Practice naming a preference

Education & practice

Knowing the facts does not always make a first sentence easy. Rehearse an opening, try another, and keep language that feels natural to you.

Try a health conversation

Pressure & fear of judgment

You might worry that a question will sound like blame or that a limit will disappoint someone. Naming your needs can help you begin; another person is still responsible for respecting your boundary.

Practice stating a boundary
